info.description:
Filings and company data for listed companies across the G20 and Europe. Send your API key in the `X-API-Key` header on every request. New here? Start with the [quickstart](https://financialfilings.com/developers/#quickstart).

**Credits.** Every call costs credits, and each endpoint below shows its price. `X-Credits-Charged` on the response says what a call cost, and `GET /usage/` shows the month so far. A free account gets a monthly allowance. Webhooks are an Enterprise feature. Pricing: https://financialfilings.com/developers/

**Rate limits.** Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Burst-Limit` (a rate such as `50/second`), `X-RateLimit-Monthly-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Monthly-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Monthly-Unit` (`requests` or `credits`). All four are strings and can be non-numeric (for example `Unlimited`); the last two are left out when they don't apply.

**Without an API key (x402).** Most read endpoints can also be paid per call in USDC on Base: a request without a key answers `402 Payment Required` with the price in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header. Terms: https://financialfilings.com/api-terms/#keyless-access. Agent directories read the paid routes from https://api.financialreports.eu/openapi.json.

Retrieve a paginated list of companies.

parameters.name: cik
parameters.description: Filter by SEC Central Index Key (CIK). Accepts padded or bare (`CIK0000320193`, `0000320193` and `320193` are equivalent). The CIK is assigned by the SEC and survives corporate renames, mergers and ticker changes, so it is the stable key for reconciling a securities universe against our coverage.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Filter by Company country ISO Alpha-2 code(s). Comma-separated for multiple values.

parameters.name: date_public_after
parameters.description: Companies last updated on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Granularity is one day (a Europe/Berlin date). For a full sync, seed the catalogue once first and partition that pass (by `countries=`, say), because offset paging stops at 50,000 rows, well short of the full catalogue. The few companies with no `date_public` yet are never returned by a date filter. A company updated while you page is re-dated, so following `next` can miss it; `date_public_cursor` cannot. De-duplicate by `id` and overlap windows by a day.

parameters.name: date_public_before
parameters.description: Companies last updated on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Granularity is one day (a Europe/Berlin date). For a full sync, seed the catalogue once first and partition that pass (by `countries=`, say), because offset paging stops at 50,000 rows, well short of the full catalogue. The few companies with no `date_public` yet are never returned by a date filter. A company updated while you page is re-dated, so following `next` can miss it; `date_public_cursor` cannot. De-duplicate by `id` and overlap windows by a day.

parameters.name: date_public_cursor
parameters.description: Resume a sync after the last company you received: `YYYY-MM-DD,<id>`, its `date_public` and `id`. Returns the companies after it in (`date_public`, `id`) order, up to and including yesterday, so today's changes arrive tomorrow. Requires `ordering=date_public`. Don't follow `next`: request page 1 again with the cursor set to the last company of each page, until a page comes back empty. Start with `<first date>,0`. A company updated mid-walk is re-dated to today and returned by a later walk, never skipped. Companies with no `date_public` are never returned.

parameters.name: ordering
parameters.description:
Sort field: `id`, `name`, `date_ipo`, `year_founded`, `country_iso__name`, `date_public` or `relevance`. Prefix with `-` for descending (e.g. `-name`).

`date_public` is the date the record last changed (Europe/Berlin). `-date_public` lists companies without one first; add `date_public_after` to leave those out.

`date_ipo` lists companies without a known IPO date last, `-date_ipo` lists them first.

With `search` or `ticker` and no `ordering`, results are ranked by relevance: exact ticker, exact name, name prefix, then fuzzy match, ties broken by filing volume. `relevance` only works with one of those two.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search across company name (including former names) and ticker symbol, and by LEI or ISIN from its start (a full code or a leading prefix such as `SE00128`). Case-insensitive, and accent-insensitive on the company name (`Hermes` matches the accented spelling). Multiple whitespace-separated terms are AND-combined (each term must match at least one of the searched fields); trailing legal forms such as `AB`, `AG`, `N.V.` or `plc` are ignored, so `EQT AB` finds `EQT`. Results are relevance-ranked unless an explicit `ordering` is supplied.

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Filter by stock Ticker symbol. Case-insensitive and separator-insensitive (`BRK.B`, `BRK-B` and `BRK B` are equivalent). Matches the company's primary ticker and its venue listings, so a secondary share class such as `GOOG` resolves to its issuer. A ticker held by several companies on different exchanges returns all of them (`count` above 1). To pin the exchange, append its ISO country code: `WDI.DE`, `1316.HK`. ISO codes, not Yahoo suffixes: `.PA`, `.SG`, `.L` and other Yahoo exchange codes are not read as a market.

Returns a company's cash dividends, one per dividend and share class, from the day the company announces them, so an upcoming dividend is listed before its ex-date. Each dividend carries its amount per share as declared, its ex, record and payment dates, and the filing that announced it. A later notice that moves a date updates the dividend and is listed in `date_changes`.

**Stated and derived dates.** Dates are as the company states them. Where a notice leaves the ex-date or record date out, it is computed from the market's settlement rule or from the company's own pattern on its past dividends, and listed with its rule in `derived_dates`; a later notice that states it replaces it.

**Amounts** are exact decimal strings, gross, per share, in the declared currency, as declared. `split_adjusted` carries the amount on today's share basis: divided by every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the notice stating the amount was published.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this company.

parameters.name: include_predecessors
parameters.description: Also serve the dividends of the company's predecessors: the issuers it succeeded by reorganisation or redomicile (its `predecessors` of kind reorganization or other on GET /companies/{id}/, followed back through the chain), each announced by a notice released up to and including the link's effective date (UTC), as `include_predecessors` does on GET /filings/. A dividend two of them hold (same kind, class, amount, currency and date) is served once, from the nearer company. `split_adjusted` then divides by the predecessors' splits too; a link states no exchange ratio, so each predecessor share counts as one share of its successor. Predecessors your plan cannot see are left out.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only dividends in this status.

status.description: `upcoming` while its ex, record or payment date is today or later (or, with no date announced yet, for 180 days after it was announced); then `paid`. Today is the date in Berlin. `cancelled` when the company withdrew it.

is_interest_on_equity.description: Brazil: interest on equity (juros sobre capital próprio).

amount.description: Gross amount per share, as declared. Not adjusted for later splits: see `split_adjusted`.

derived_dates.description: Dates computed from a market or company rule instead of stated in a notice, each with its rule.

date_changes.description: Dates (and an amount restated after a split) a later notice changed, with the filing that changed them.

split_adjusted.description: The amount on today's share basis: divided (per-share figures) or multiplied (share counts) by `adjustment_factor`, the product of `ratio_new / ratio_old` of every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the filing the value was read from was published. A filing published after a split already states the new basis, so it is not adjusted again. `adjustment_factor` `1` and no `split_event_ids`: nothing to adjust. Rights issues and spin-offs are not adjusted. `value` is null, with `null_reason`, when the filing predates our split history (1990), when two events that cannot both be right would apply, when a split that applies is not served to you, near the record date of a split whose ex-date no notice states, for a period-end share count or book value per share with a split between the period end and the publication, or for a standalone quarter derived from filings published either side of a split.

derived_dates.ex_date: ex-date = 2 trading sessions before payment, the company's pattern on its past dividends
derived_dates.record_date: T+2 settlement: ex-date = 1 session before the record date

---
**Experimental:** the response may change without an API version bump.

**Per-share values are not split-adjusted unless you ask.** EPS, book value per share and share counts, in `periods` and in `standalone_quarters`, are on the share basis of the filing they come from, so a series that spans a stock split is not comparable as served. Pass `include=split_adjusted` for each figure on today's share basis. On `/companies/{id}/dividends/` the `split_adjusted` block is always included, next to the as-declared `amount`; here it is opt-in.

Returns a company's standardized income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement: `periods`, each holding its `statements`, each holding `line_items`. Use `depth` and `parent_code` on each line item to rebuild the statement hierarchy.

**One statement per period.** When several filings report the same fiscal year, period and statement type, one is selected. A filing with the company's own financials beats one without (such as an employee benefit plan's report), the company's reporting currency beats another currency, and a complete statement beats a fragment. Only then does the latest filing win. A selected statement in a currency other than the company's carries `currency_mismatch: true`.

**Currency is never converted.** `currency` is the currency the company presented in. A company that switches currency does not restate earlier years, so compare `currency.code` across periods before aggregating. A line item with its own `currency` comes from a dual-currency filing.

**Values.** `value` and `raw_value` are exact decimal strings: parse them with a decimal type. `raw_value` and `scale` are `null` when a figure was computed rather than read off the page. `confidence` is set only where an independent check re-derived the figure and agreed: `null` means unjudged, not low confidence. `source_page` is the page of the filing's PDF a value read from that PDF is printed on, `null` where it is not known.

**Source.** Each statement names its `source_filing`, with `document_url` and `viewer_url` to the document. The full `sources` list, including candidates that were not selected, is only returned to accounts with it enabled; `sources_masked` says which applies.

**Not the bulk dataset.** Comparative statements, restatements, quality flags and stable row ids are only in the S3 `line_items/` delivery. `is_comparative` says whether the selected figures came from a later report's prior-year column.

**Price and history.** One call costs the same however many periods or line items come back. An account limited to a rolling history window gets a `history_window` object; its `max_history_days` is the limit.

parameters.name: as_known_at
parameters.description: Values as we held them at this time (ISO-8601 datetime, e.g. `2026-10-20T12:00:00Z`; a datetime without an offset is UTC; a bare date `YYYY-MM-DD` means the end of that day in UTC). Each value we corrected or deleted since is served as it was then, a value first written since is left out, and each period's statement is then selected from those values under today's selection rules. Filings not yet released at that time are left out. Combines with `as_of`. History starts at 2026-10-19T17:05:18Z: an earlier time returns `400`; a future time is read as now. Statements are judged and ranked on what we held about them then (company, primary period, currency, filing type, title, release time): a statement moved to another company since is served and flagged `withdrawn_reason`; one moved to this company since is left out. Not reconstructed: period relabels, statements from filings removed since, and the `extraction` block, which is served as it is today. `updated_at` is capped at this time.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Filing-date point-in-time cutoff (`YYYY-MM-DD`), for all history: each period is served from the filings we hold that were released on or before `as_of`, so no figure from a later filing is served. Example: with `as_of=2025-03-01`, FY2024 of a company that published its annual report on 2025-03-20 is served from what was out by 2025-03-01 (an earnings release, if we hold one), or not at all. The cutoff is a UTC date on the filing's release time: a regulator that dates filings without a time of day is stored at midnight (UTC, or local midnight in mainland China, so a filing dated D in Beijing counts from D-1 UTC). A filing whose own period had not ended by its release date is left out with all its statements: mostly that date is a placeholder, not when it was published. The filing set is point-in-time; our reading of each filing is current: figures are corrected in place, so each value is today's reading of a filing released by `as_of`. Use `include=first_reported` for each period's figures as the filing that first reported it stated them, each line item's `updated_at` to see when a value last changed, and `as_known_at` for the values as we held them at a past time. That change log starts 2026-10-19: for an earlier `as_of`, values can reflect corrections made later, and `as_known_at` cannot undo them.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
**Per-share figures and share counts are as reported, on each filing's own share basis: pass `split_adjusted` for a series comparable across stock splits.**

Comma-separated. `revisions` adds a `revisions` list to every line item: each recorded change to that value, oldest first, with `old_value` -> `new_value` and a reason category. With `as_known_at`, only the changes up to that time. `preliminary` adds `preliminary_results`: the company's own preliminary figures, published before the report and labelled preliminary, never merged into `periods`. `as_reported` adds `as_reported` to a standardised total read straight from the filer's XBRL whose calculation tree ties: the face lines it is made of, as the filer tagged them. Not served with `as_known_at`. `standalone_quarters` adds `standalone_quarters`: one three-month period per fiscal quarter (H2 for half-year reporters), income statement and cash flow, derived from year-to-date interims where the company reports no three-month figure, each value flagged `reported`, `derived` or `derived_approx`, never merged into `periods`. `split_adjusted` adds `split_adjusted` to every per-share figure (EPS, book value per share) and share count, in `periods` and `standalone_quarters`: the value on today's share basis (or `as_of`'s), next to the unchanged as-reported `value`, with its `adjustment_factor` and the `split_event_ids` from `/companies/{id}/splits/` it applies. Recomputed on every request, so a split re-adjusts history the day it takes effect. Not served with `as_known_at`. `ratios` adds `ratios`: per served fiscal year, fundamental ratios (margins, returns, leverage with and without lease liabilities, liquidity, turnover, growth, cash payout, per share and per employee) computed from the values `periods` serves, each with its `inputs` and `source_filing_ids`, or `null` with a `null_reason`. No ratios on share prices. `first_reported` adds `first_reported` to every statement: the period's figures as the filing that first reported the period as its own stated them, with that filing's id and release time; `null` where no filing did (a period held only as a later report's prior-year column, or a derived one). `vintages` adds `vintages` to every statement: every filing's own figures for the period, oldest first, the original report, later reports of the same period and stored prior-year columns. Omitted, like `sources`, when `sources_masked` is true. Both pass the same withholds as `periods`: a value withheld there is `null` here.

parameters.name: include_predecessors
parameters.description: Also serve the statements of the company's predecessors: the issuers it succeeded by reorganisation or redomicile (its `predecessors` of kind reorganization or other on GET /companies/{id}/, followed back through the chain), each from filings released up to and including the link's effective date (UTC), as `include_predecessors` does on GET /filings/. Each company is selected on its own statements; the requested company's win their periods, and a predecessor fills only periods no nearer company serves. `source_filing` names the filing each statement came from. Predecessors your plan cannot see are left out. With `include=split_adjusted`, values are adjusted by the predecessors' splits too, as GET /companies/{id}/splits/?include_predecessors=true serves them; a link states no exchange ratio, so each predecessor share counts as one share of its successor. Not combined with `as_known_at`, `include=preliminary` or `include=standalone_quarters` (`400`).

parameters.name: include_withheld_grades
parameters.description: Also serve line items of grade `withheld` (a tier measured below 50% accurate). Without it they are left out, and `trust_grade_withheld` counts them. Cannot be combined with `include=preliminary`, `include=ratios` or `include=standalone_quarters`.

parameters.name: line_items
parameters.description: Comma-separated KPI codes to include (e.g. `revenue,ebitda,net_income_loss`). Omit to return all extracted line items. Statements with none of the requested codes are dropped. Unknown codes return `400`; see `/line-item-definitions/`.

parameters.name: min_trust_grade
parameters.description: Serve only line items of at least this `trust_grade`, best first: `platinum`, `gold`, `silver`, `bronze`. A tier's grade comes from its published accuracy (`/companies/financials/trust-tiers/`); `xbrl` is platinum by definition. A line item with no grade (no tier, or `derived` / `xbrl-derived`, not measured) is left out whenever this is set, and so is a value served null for another reason (it has no grade either). Cannot be combined with `include=preliminary`, `include=ratios` or `include=standalone_quarters`.

parameters.name: min_trust_tier
parameters.description: Serve only line items of at least this `trust_tier`, best first: `xbrl` (the issuer's own XBRL tag), `verified`, `accepted`, `review`. A line item with no tier, or of tier `derived` or `xbrl-derived` (not measured), is left out whenever this is set; a kept line item that is withheld for another reason is still served null with its `withheld_reason`. Without it every value is served with its tier. Cannot be combined with `include=preliminary`, `include=ratios` or `include=standalone_quarters`, which are computed from values this filter would leave out. Each tier's measured accuracy: `/companies/financials/trust-tiers/`.

parameters.name: statement_type
parameters.description: Filter to a single statement type.

template.description: The company's KPI template. Banks and insurers also get their template's own line items, and are not served the industrial-only ones; see `templates` on /api/line-item-definitions/ for which items are meaningful for it.

sources_masked.description: True when your account does not have source identities unlocked. Then `sources` is omitted from every statement.

as_known_at.description: The instant values were reconstructed at, in UTC: a bare date is echoed as the end of that day, a future time as now.

trust_grade_withheld.description: Line items of grade `withheld` left out of `periods` (0 with `include_withheld_grades=true`). Withheld values still count as readings when other values are checked against each other.

currency_mismatch.description: True when this statement's currency differs from the company's modal reporting currency: the code held by more than 60% of the statements we serve for that company. When no code clears 60% (a genuinely dual-currency issuer, or one mid-transition) there is no modal currency and this is `false` on every statement, including the off-currency ones. A data-quality signal, not provenance, so it is returned even when `sources_masked` is true. It compares a statement against its company's history; it does not mean the statement itself mixes currencies.

accounting_standard.description: The accounting standard the statement was prepared under. National standards that are IFRS word for word (K-IFRS, TIFRS, HKFRS, SFRS(I), AASB, ...) are `IFRS`; ones with carve-outs or only converged (Ind AS, CAS, SAK, JMIS, any national GAAP) are `LOCAL_GAAP`. `UNKNOWN` when neither the filing nor its market says; null on statements not yet classified. See `accounting_standard_basis` for how it is known.

accounting_standard_basis.description: How `accounting_standard` is known. `xbrl_taxonomy`: read from the filing's own XBRL (a declared standard, or the standard taxonomy its facts are tagged in). `market_default`: not read from the filing; the standard listed companies in its home market must use for consolidated accounts, so an issuer with an exemption may differ. `filer_stated` and `document_stated` are reserved. Null when the standard is `UNKNOWN` or not yet classified.

consolidation_basis.description: `consolidated`: the group accounts, the parent and its subsidiaries. `standalone`: one company's own accounts without its subsidiaries (a parent's separate accounts, or a company that has none). Read from the scope the filer declares in its own XBRL, or, for a statement without XBRL, taken from the filer's XBRL statement for the same period that its figures agree with, where the filer tags both. Null means unknown, not consolidated: most statements without XBRL, and XBRL that does not state a scope. A company may be served one basis in some years and the other in others, so compare it across periods before comparing values. A data-quality signal, not provenance, so it is returned even when `sources_masked` is true.

model.description: How the statement was read: `xbrl-native@<version>` from the filer's own XBRL, `document-extraction@<date>` from the filing document. Match on the prefix; the suffix is a version.

prompt_version.description: The extractor version: the XBRL engine's version, or the date of the document extractor's version.

statement_type.description: The KPI's home statement in the taxonomy, which can differ from the statement it was extracted onto. `SUP` appears here but is never a statement type.

value.description: Value in absolute units, as an exact decimal string, not a number. Parse with a decimal type; float loses precision at financial magnitudes. Null when the figure was withheld: as unrecoverable; where `total_current_liabilities` exceeds `total_liabilities` in the statement it is served in, as whichever of the two `total_assets` less `total_equity` contradicts (both where it cannot tell); as `total_liabilities_and_equity` equal to `total_equity` and short of a `total_assets` the other lines add up to, as `total_liabilities` that is the non-current liabilities, or as a current total of a US GAAP balance sheet that presents none. A withheld line keeps its place in the statement.

raw_value.description: The figure as printed in the document, as an exact decimal string. When non-null, `value == raw_value * multiplier(scale)` to rounding (within 1% or 0.01). Null, together with `scale`, when `value` is null, when `value` was computed from other line items rather than read from the document (e.g. `net_debt` recomputed from the figures served beside it), or whenever `raw_value * scale` does not reproduce `value` (e.g. a value rescaled against the company's other filings), because then the printed figure is no longer the value's provenance. A printed total that is missing some of its components keeps its `raw_value`, because the printed figure is still its provenance. On a statement a language model read (`extraction.model` not `xbrl-native`), `raw_value` is the figure the model returned, which can be a total it computed from other lines rather than one the document prints.

scale.description: Reporting scale of `raw_value`. Withheld with it.

currency.description: The value's own currency code, which may differ from the statement's reporting currency for per-share figures. Null for ratios.

confidence.description: Confidence that this value is the figure the document states, or null where nothing has judged it. Non-null only where a second, independent check of the filing agreed with the extracted value; the number is that check's probability for the figure it picked. Null does not mean low confidence: it means unjudged, which is every value not yet checked and every value sent for review. Treat it as a filter, not a score: branch on non-null, do not compare nulls.

source_page.description: The 1-based page of the source filing's PDF the value is printed on, for a value read from the PDF rather than from XBRL. Null when it is not known: the document is not a PDF (XBRL, HTML), the value could not be placed on exactly one page, or the value served is computed or withheld rather than the printed figure (`raw_value` is then null too).

confirmed.description: True where a second, independent source agrees with this value (within 0.5%): for a value read from the report, a second extraction of the same filing; for a value that fills a gap in the report's own statements, a value extracted elsewhere in the company's filings. Null otherwise: no second source, or one that does not agree. Null does not mean wrong. Always null for a value read from the filing's XBRL: that class has no second reading, and judged blind on its own it is the most precise one we serve (~98% right). Always null under `as_known_at`: confirmation is not reconstructed as of a past time.

confirmed_precision.description: How often values confirmed this way were right when judged blind (0.975 for a second extraction agreeing, 0.93 for an extracted value agreeing with a filled gap): a rate for the class, not a probability for this value. Null when `confirmed` is null.

trust_tier.description: How the value was read, best first. `xbrl`: the issuer's own XBRL tag (as tagged, or with only its sign or scale normalised). `xbrl-derived`: calculated by us from the issuer's XBRL tags (a total built from tagged components). `verified`: read from the report by AI, accepted by our claim check and confirmed by an independent check of its scale, unit, period and scope. `accepted`: read by AI and accepted by the claim check, not verified. `review`: read by AI where the claim check did not accept it. `derived`: calculated from AI-read values. Null: any other value (a statement extracted by an earlier method, a total we built from tagged components) or a null value. Filter with `min_trust_tier`.

trust_tier_accuracy.description: The measured accuracy of the value's `trust_tier`: how often values of that tier matched the issuer's own XBRL in a pre-registered sample. A rate for the class, not a probability for this value. Null for a tier not measured. Method and sample sizes: `/companies/financials/trust-tiers/`.

trust_grade.description: The value's grade, from its `trust_tier`'s measured accuracy: `platinum` at least 97%, `gold` 90-97%, `silver` 80-90%, `bronze` 50-80%, `withheld` below 50% (served only with `include_withheld_grades=true`). `xbrl` is platinum by definition (the filer's own tag). Null: not graded (no tier, or a tier not measured). A grade for the class, not for this value. Filter with `min_trust_grade`; bands and rates: `/companies/financials/trust-tiers/`.

withheld_reason.description: Present only when `value` is null because the figure is a derived or analytic line (net debt, cash and short-term investments, capitalisation, debt issued or repaid, intangibles, retained earnings, ...) that no second source confirms and that is not the filer's own XBRL reading. `derived_unconfirmed`. The statement keeps the line; `raw_value`, `scale`, `source_page` and `confidence` are null with it. Absent on every other value.

revisions.description: Present only with `include=revisions`: every recorded change to this value, oldest first (with `as_known_at`, up to that time). Empty when none was recorded. Recording started 2026-10-19T17:05:18Z; `pre_recording` entries are older corrections whose `changed_at` is approximate (the change happened at or before it).

op.description: `insert`: first written. `update`: corrected. `delete`: removed (it may be written again by a later `insert`). `pre_recording`: a correction from before recording started, approximate time.

old_value.description: `value` before the change; null on insert.

new_value.description: `value` after the change; null on delete. A change to another field of the value (its as-reported figure, currency or statement) has old_value == new_value.

reason.description: `extraction`: (re-)extraction from the document. `cleanup`: an automated rule-based correction. `repair`: a correction pass run by our team. `manual`: a hand edit. `unknown`: not recorded.

withdrawn_reason.description: Present only with `as_known_at`, and only on a statement (and on its values) that was served for this company at that time and is not served for it today because it was withdrawn: `reattributed`: the statement now belongs to another company record, where it may be served; `purged`: reserved, its filing was removed altogether (not served yet; the filing's type, release time and links would be null unless recorded). Absent everywhere else.

as_reported.description: Present only with `include=as_reported`, and only on a total read straight from one fact of the filer's XBRL (not derived, not adjusted) whose own calculation tree adds up beneath it, at the statement's primary period: the face lines the total is made of, as the filer tagged them. `value` = sum(`weight` x line `value`) + `other` over the lines that have `codes`; the lines without codes add up to `other` within the filer's rounding. Not the `raw_value` / `scale` pair, which is this value as printed. Absent on comparative-period values, derived or adjusted values, filings whose tree does not add up, and with `as_known_at`.

other.description: The part of `value` the lines with `codes` do not explain: `value` - sum(`weight` x their `value`).

label.description: The line's label as the filer presents it.

value.description: The line's value in the filing, in the sign the filer tagged it.

weight.description: +1 or -1: how the line enters this value as served. The filer's calculation weight, flipped when the value is served in the opposite sign to its tag (an outflow tagged positive, served negative).

codes.description: The line item codes this line is read into; empty when it is part of `other`.

split_adjusted.description: The value on today's share basis: divided (per-share figures) or multiplied (share counts) by `adjustment_factor`, the product of `ratio_new / ratio_old` of every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the filing the value was read from was published. A filing published after a split already states the new basis, so it is not adjusted again. `adjustment_factor` `1` and no `split_event_ids`: nothing to adjust. Rights issues and spin-offs are not adjusted. `value` is null, with `null_reason`, when the filing predates our split history (1990), when two events that cannot both be right would apply, when a split that applies is not served to you, near the record date of a split whose ex-date no notice states, for a period-end share count or book value per share with a split between the period end and the publication, or for a standalone quarter derived from filings published either side of a split.

updated_at.description: When this value was last written. Equal to the extraction time for an untouched value; moves when a later correction pass rewrites the value in place (a re-extraction replaces the whole statement and sets a new one). Compare it with the value from your previous poll to detect a changed figure without diffing. It does not move when a whole statement is withdrawn or when a different filing starts supplying the period; watch `source_filing` for that.

available_at.description: When the filing this value was read from was released. Usually the statement's own `source_filing.release_datetime`. Later where the value was filled in from another filing because the selected statement lacks it (named in `extraction.notes`): for example a prior-year figure taken from the next annual report. For a point-in-time series, drop values whose `available_at` is after your cutoff, or pass `as_of`, which never serves a value from a filing released after it.

withdrawn_reason.description: Present only with `as_known_at`, and only on a statement (and on its values) that was served for this company at that time and is not served for it today because it was withdrawn: `reattributed`: the statement now belongs to another company record, where it may be served; `purged`: reserved, its filing was removed altogether (not served yet; the filing's type, release time and links would be null unless recorded). Absent everywhere else.

is_comparative.description: True when this period was read from the comparative (prior-year) column of a later report, because no report presented it as its own period. A data-quality signal, not provenance, so it is returned even when `sources_masked` is true.

filing_type.description: Our own normalised filing-type code, not the publishing authority's label.

document_url.description: Direct link to our hosted copy of the document. Null in the rare case we hold no document for the filing.

viewer_url.description: Link to the document on our own platform.

is_selected.description: Exactly one entry per statement is the selected one.

sources.description: Every filing that reported this (period, statement_type), including the candidates selection rejected and any filing whose values filled in the selected statement. Omitted when `sources_masked` is true. The selected filing is always available as `source_filing`.

is_comparative.description: The filing reported this period as a prior-year column, not as its own period.

withheld_reason.description: Present only when `value` is null. `derived_unconfirmed`: as in `periods`. `scale_conflict`: the filing's figure sits a power of ten (10x, 100x, ...) from the figure `periods` serves for the line, so one of the two readings is mis-scaled; it is refused, not corrected. Never on per-share figures or share counts.

first_reported.description: Present only with `include=first_reported`. The figures for this period and statement as the filing that first reported the period as its own stated them: of the filings presenting the period as their own that count as the company's own report (not a later report's prior-year column, a fragment, another entity's filing, the parent's separate accounts where the group's exist, or an amendment), the one released first. That filing's own values only: no value filled in from another filing. `release_datetime` is when they became public, to the time of day where the regulator gives one. `null` where no filing reported the period as its own.

Never on per-share figures or share counts.

is_own_report.description: The filing reports the period as its own and counts as the company's own report, the filings `first_reported` is picked from. False for a prior-year column, a fragment, a filing in another currency than the company reports in, the parent's separate accounts where the group's exist, a non-report document or an amendment.

vintages.description: Present only with `include=vintages`, and omitted when `sources_masked` is true. Every filing's own figures for this period and statement, oldest first: the original report, later reports of the same period (an earnings release, then the annual report; a re-filed report) and stored prior-year columns of later reports (`is_comparative`; annual periods only). For filings read from the filer's XBRL we store the filing's own period, so a later restatement there is mostly not listed. Per-share figures are as reported: `include=split_adjusted` adjusts `periods` only.

preliminary_results.description: Present only with `include=preliminary`. The company's own preliminary results figures, published before the report for the period and expected to differ from it (today: Korean 잠정실적 notices). Never merged into `periods`. One entry per notice and period, corrections included, so the history is point in time: `is_latest` marks the newest notice for its period and basis among those returned.

unit.description: The scale the notice printed, e.g. 억원.

standalone_quarters.description: Present only with `include=standalone_quarters`. One three-month period per fiscal quarter (a six-month `H2` for a company that reports half years only), income statement and cash flow, newest first. `reported` values are the company's own three-month figures; `derived` values are differences of its reported year-to-date figures (`formula`, e.g. `H1 - Q1`, and the `source_filing_ids` they rest on); `derived_approx` is EPS as the difference of year-to-date EPS, given only when the weighted share count moved less than 2%. A value that cannot be derived safely is `null` with a `null_reason`. `periods` stays exactly as reported.

split_adjusted.description: The value on today's share basis: divided (per-share figures) or multiplied (share counts) by `adjustment_factor`, the product of `ratio_new / ratio_old` of every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the filing the value was read from was published. Rights issues and spin-offs are not adjusted. `value` is null, with `null_reason`, when the filing predates our split history (1990), when two events that cannot both be right would apply, when a split that applies is not served to you, near the record date of a split whose ex-date no notice states, for a period-end share count or book value per share with a split between the period end and the publication, or for a standalone quarter derived from filings published either side of a split.

balance_sheet.description: The balance sheet `periods` serves at this period's `period_end_date`, as reported (a balance sheet is never derived). `periods` serves one balance sheet per date, under the longest period ending on it, so a US quarterly report's is there under `H1` or `9M`; here it is on `Q2` or `Q3`. Empty when no balance sheet is served at that date.

value.description: Decimal string, absolute units, as served in `periods`.

split_adjusted.description: The value on today's share basis: divided (per-share figures) or multiplied (share counts) by `adjustment_factor`, the product of `ratio_new / ratio_old` of every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the filing the value was read from was published. A filing published after a split already states the new basis, so it is not adjusted again. `adjustment_factor` `1` and no `split_event_ids`: nothing to adjust. ratios.description: Present only with `include=ratios`. One entry per served fiscal year (`FY`), newest first, each with the same ratios in a fixed order, computed from the values `periods` serves for that year (fiscal-year-end balances, never averaged; no ratios on share prices). Each ratio lists the served `inputs` it was built from and their `source_filing_ids`. A ratio that cannot be built is `null` with a `null_reason`. Fractions are decimals (0.12 = 12%); `currency` is set only for amounts (net debt, per share, per employee).

Returns a company's stock splits, reverse splits and bonus issues, newest first, including splits that are announced but not yet effective. Each split is one event, however many notices the company published about it (proposal, approval, record date, completion).

**Ratio.** `ratio_new:ratio_old` is shares after to shares before, in lowest terms: a 4-for-1 split is `4:1`, a 1-for-10 reverse split `1:10`, a bonus issue of one new share for every two held `3:2`. `factor` is the same ratio as one number.

**Dates** are as the company or its exchange stated them; a date that was not stated is `null`, never estimated.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this company.

parameters.name: include_predecessors
parameters.description: Also serve the splits of the company's predecessors: the issuers it succeeded by reorganisation or redomicile (its `predecessors` of kind reorganization or other on GET /companies/{id}/, followed back through the chain), each dated up to and including the link's effective date. A split two of them hold (same type, ratio and date) is served once, from the nearer company. A link states no exchange ratio, so each predecessor share counts as one share of its successor. Predecessors your plan cannot see are left out.

parameters.description: Only splits with this status.

id.description: Stable id of the split event.

split_type.description: `split` (incl. face-value splits), `reverse` (share consolidation) or `bonus` (bonus / capitalisation issue, stock dividend).

ratio_new.description: Shares held after the split for every `ratio_old` shares held before.

factor.description: `ratio_new / ratio_old`: 4 for a 4-for-1 split, 0.1 for a 1-for-10 reverse split, 2 for a 1:1 bonus issue. Divide per-share values before the ex-date by it to restate them on the post-split basis.

Duplicate-company merges, oldest first.

When two records turn out to describe the same issuer we retire one and keep the other. The retired id disappears from the company list, so a warehouse built by incremental sync would otherwise keep the stale row forever. Poll this feed to reconcile.

**Poll `updated_at_from`, not `merged_at_from`.** Merges can be reversed, and a reversal edits the existing record in place rather than adding a new one: it moves `updated_at` but never `merged_at`. A `reversed_at` on a record you already ingested means the merge no longer holds and `shell_id` is a live company again.

Results are ordered by `merged_at` then `id`, so paging is stable even when a bulk merge writes several records in the same instant. Records are never deleted from this feed.

Covers merges recorded since 2026-06-29. Earlier cleanups predate this log and are not represented; companies removed by hard deletion rather than merge do not appear here either.

Match a list of your identifiers to our companies in one request.

Each row can carry any mix of `isin`, `lei`, `cik`, `ticker` and `name`, plus an optional `ref` that is echoed back so you can join results to your rows. Results come back in input order.

**Resolution order:** ISIN, LEI, CIK, ticker, venue ticker, name. The first hit wins, but every identifier you send is checked: if two point to different companies, the row is `ambiguous` with `identifier_conflict` and both in `candidates`.

**A name alone never returns `matched`.** A name-only row is at best `ambiguous`, with candidates to choose from.

**Tickers are checked against your `name`.** Tickers are reused across exchanges, so your name can pick the company that holds the ticker on another venue. A row matched only through a venue ticker is `ambiguous` + `name_disagrees` when the name disagrees, and `matched` + `security_listing_unverified` when you sent no name. If other companies hold the same ticker elsewhere, the row carries `multiple_tickers` and lists them in `candidates`. Add a country code (`WDI.DE`) to pin the exchange.

**Billing:** one request is one call, whatever the row count.

Up to 500 rows per request. Up to 50 rows that need a name lookup get one, within 25 seconds; rows resolved by an identifier don't count. Past either limit, a name-only row returns `not_covered` with `name_tier_skipped`, so split large name-heavy batches.

Companions are small machine-readable XBRL/XML/JSON files stored beside a report for financial extraction, typed like that report. Most are not converted to markdown and show processing_status SKIPPED; the report beside them carries the text. Default false: type, types, category and categories return the reports only.

Prefix with '-' for descending order (e.g., `-release_datetime`). Rows that tie on the chosen field are ordered by `id` in the same direction, so paging through results with `next` does not repeat or skip a filing as long as the matching filings do not change while you page. `-filing_type_confidence` lists filings without a score first; add `min_confidence=0` to leave those out.

A phrase of two or more words also matches where the conversion split it across lines, table cells or pages, or ran its words together. Filters that can be combined with it: `added_to_platform_from`, `added_to_platform_to`, `companies`, `company`, `company_isin`, `countries`, `include_companions`, `include_predecessors`, `language`, `languages`, `lei`, `release_datetime_from`, `release_datetime_to`, `source`, `sources`, `type`, `types`. Any other filter, and `search` (the company/title name match on `GET /filings/`), returns 400 `filter_not_supported_with_q`.
- `q` is repeatable and its values are alternatives, OR-ed: pass translations and synonyms in the filing languages (`q=buyback&q=share repurchase&q=自社株買い`). At most 5 values, each at most 200 characters.
- `type`/`types` also take regulator form names (`10-Q`, `8-K`, `S-1`, `20-F`): each is searched as the FinancialFilings type(s) its filings are filed under, and `search.types_resolved` says which, with `widens` when those types hold other filings too and `may_miss` when some filings of the form are under a type not included. A code with no mapping returns 400.
- `companies` = up to 50 company ids, comma-separated (with `include_predecessors`, each one's predecessors too, as with `company`).
- `group_by=company` returns one row per company instead of filings: `company_id`, `company_name`, `country_code`, `isin` (primary, or null), `hit_count`, `first_release_datetime`, `last_release_datetime` and `best_filing_id`, best match first, paged like filings. The rows are counted over the first `max_results` matching filings you can see (`search.filings_grouped`), not over every match: with `search.capped` true, counts may be higher and more companies may exist (`search.message`). No `match` snippets; `ordering` is refused. Billed as one page.
- With a `languages` or `countries` filter, a `q` value that is a known finance term ("going concern", "share buyback", "profit warning", "cyberattack"...) is also searched in those filing languages, from a fixed list, weighted below your own terms. `search.expanded_terms` lists what was added. Without either filter, only what you send is searched: send the term in each language yourself.
- Every word of a `q` value must occur (matching folds case and accents and word stems). When a value of 6 or more words matches nothing, the search is retried with 70% of its words, and `search.relaxed_note` says so: prefer short key terms, one per value.
- Results are ordered by relevance (best match first) unless `ordering` is given.
- Only the first `max_results` matches by relevance are paged (default 1000; send `max_results` from 1 to 1000 to change it, up to 10000 on Enterprise and pay-as-you-go plans; a value above your plan's limit is lowered to it, and `search.max_results_note` says so; echoed in `search.max_results`): `count` is the number of those you can see (at most `max_results`); when `search.scan_complete` is false it is a lower bound, not the visible total. `search.capped` true means more matching filings MAY exist beyond what this endpoint pages. `search.scan_complete` false means the scan stopped before checking every candidate (a larger `max_results` gets the same time to scan, so it is more likely to stop early); an EMPTY page with `scan_complete` false is NOT an absence: narrow `q` or the filters and search again. A page past the first `max_results` returns 400 `search_page_past_cap`: narrow `q` or the filters, or raise `max_results`. Each page is billed the same whatever `max_results` is.
- Each result carries `match`, snippets from its text: `{query, hits, total_hits}` with the `q` value that was found literally; `{"query": null, "hits": [], "total_hits": 0}` when the text was read but no value occurs literally (it matched through stemming, accent folding or word segmentation); `null` when snippets were not computed (results after the first 10 of a page, or text that could not be read in time). Neither `null` nor 0 means the filing did not match. `match.truncated` is true when the filing is longer than the 20 MB the index reads, so a match past that point is not found.
- 503 `search_unavailable` when the full-text index cannot be reached; retry later. 503 `search_too_slow` when the search's filters and matches make it too heavy to answer in time: narrow `q` or the filters, or lower `max_results`. Neither is billed.
- At most 5 searches run at a time per account; a search over that usually waits up to 10 seconds for one to finish (at once when too many are already waiting), then is a 429 `search_busy`: retry after `Retry-After` seconds. Not billed.

Billed as one Markdown request per page, at the price in the Cost line, only when the page has at least one result; a page with no results bills nothing (on a plan metered in requests it still counts as one request).

Major-shareholding notices as rows: one row per reporting person, with voting and dispositive power, the aggregate owned and the percent of the class. The persons on one notice often count the same shares (a fund and its manager, the members of a group), so do not add one notice's rows up. US: Schedule 13D and 13G and their amendments, in the structured form required since 18 December 2024.

Filter by issuer (`company`, `company_isin`, `lei`, `countries`), `regime`, `holder_ref`, the event date or the publication date.

Each row names `filing_id` and `release_datetime`: GET /filings/{filing_id}/ is the notice it was read from. The issuer is the filing's company. An amendment's rows (`is_amendment`) sit next to the original's, not in place of them, so drop one of the two before adding up. Coverage: US filings published from the endpoint's launch; history is being added. Values are as reported; fields a market does not report are empty.

Null when the company has no class under the current OICS version, including entity types that carry none (funds, shells, financing vehicles). CompanyOics.description:
A company's label under the Open Industry Classification Standard (OICS): its primary class with the
class's sector, industry group and industry, its entity type and up to two secondary classes. OICS
v0.4: codes can still change before v1.0.

code.description: Primary class code: the class's place in the tree, SECTOR.GROUP.INDUSTRY.CLASS (e.g. `TC.SC.SEM.CHP`). Null for an entity type that carries no class.

name.description: Primary class name. Null when `code` is.

sector.description: The class's sector. Null when `code` is.

group.description: The class's industry group. Null when `code` is.

industry.description: The class's industry. Null when `code` is.

entity_type.description: What kind of entity the company is, decided before its activity: OPERATING, HOLDING, FUND, SPAC_SHELL, FINANCING_VEHICLE or PUBLIC_SECTOR. FUND, SPAC_SHELL, FINANCING_VEHICLE and PUBLIC_SECTOR carry no class; a HOLDING carries one only when most of its value sits in one business.

secondaries.description: Up to two further classes the company has a material business in. Never the primary.

basis.description: What the label rests on: `revenue` (reported revenue by segment or product), `filings` (other figures from the company's filings) or `description` (the company's description). `nav` (a holding's net asset value) is reserved and not written yet. How labels are assigned: /oics/methodology/.

taxonomy_version.description: OICS version the label was decided under, as major.minor, e.g. `0.4`.

classified_at.description: When the label was last written (ISO 8601, UTC).

contested.description: True when an independent second reading disagreed with the label: of the company's description, for a label with basis `description`, or a second mapping of its revenue lines, for a label decided on reported revenue. The label stands; `alternate` is the other reading. A label decided on other figures from the company's filings is never contested.

alternate.description: The other reading of a contested label: a class, or an entity type (`code` is then e.g. `HOLDING`). Information only: it is not a second classification and no filter matches it. Null when the label is not contested.

CompanyResolveMatch.description: The company on a resolve result, with its primary ticker.

ticker.description: The company's primary ticker. Secondary share classes live on the security-listings endpoint, not here.

isins.description: Primary ISIN(s). Use the company detail endpoint for the full list.

CompanyResolveResponse.description: Resolve results: `summary` counts plus one `results` entry per request row, in request order. Not paginated.

input.description: The identifiers supplied for this row, echoed back.

status.description:
`matched`: resolved to exactly one company. `matched_via_alias`: a name-only row whose name is a recorded former or alternative name of exactly one company; see `company`. `ambiguous`: several plausible companies, see `candidates`. `not_covered`: no company found.

* `matched` - Resolved to exactly one company
* `matched_via_alias` - Name is a recorded former or alternative name of exactly one company
* `ambiguous` - Several plausible companies; see candidates
* `not_covered` - No company found

resolved_via.description:
Which identifier produced the match. Null unless `status` is `matched`. Also null for `matched_via_alias`, where the name produced it.

* `isin` - ISIN
* `lei` - Legal Entity Identifier
* `cik` - SEC Central Index Key
* `ticker` - Primary ticker
* `security_listing` - Venue ticker via security listing

warnings.description: Stable codes qualifying the result. `no_identifiers`: the row carried nothing to match on. `identifier_conflict`: two identifiers on this row resolved to different companies; both are in `candidates`. `name_disagrees`: a ticker matched but the supplied name shares no distinguishing token with ours, so the match is not asserted. `multiple_tickers`: the ticker maps to more than one company. On an `ambiguous` result they are the `candidates`; on a `matched` result the company holds it as its primary ticker and the `candidates` hold it on other venues. `security_listing_unverified`: matched on a venue ticker with no name supplied, so the match could not be corroborated. ingest_lag_hours.description: Hours between publication (`release_datetime`, or for a few sources `dissemination_datetime`) and the filing reaching the platform, to one decimal. Null when the filing has no `release_datetime`. Negative when the source dates the filing in the future.

document_url.description: Direct link to our hosted copy of the original filing document (e.g. PDF). The link is not signed and does not expire: anyone holding it can download the file, so treat it like a share link. It returns 404 if the filing is later removed or its document replaced. Processed content is served differently: markdown requires an API key and HTML is served through short-lived signed links.

source_url.description: Original public link for the filing at the source authority. Null unless the webhook owner's account has source identities unlocked, the source is anonymised, or no stable link exists.

source_filing_type.description: The source authority's own classification label, verbatim. Null when the source publishes no label, it was not captured, or the source is anonymised. Not gated on source identities.

source.description: The same object as `source` on GET /filings/{id}/. Unless the webhook owner's account has source identities unlocked, `name` is a generic label and `url` is null; `id` is always the real source id (the manifests' `source_id`). Null when the filing has no source.

markdown_content.description: The full, processed content of the filing in Markdown format. This field is only included if your webhook is configured with 'include_markdown: true' and the event type is 'filing.processed'. It is null for 'filing.received'. Even with 'include_markdown: true' on a 'filing.processed' event, this field is null unless the webhook owner's plan includes filing markdown, the same check as GET /filings/{id}/markdown/.

WebhookReplayResponse.description: Result of a request to replay a delivery.

message.description: Human-readable description of the replay outcome.

secret_key.description: The unique secret key for the webhook. This is shown only once.

WebhookTestResponse.description: Result of a test delivery. Same shape on success (200) and failure (400).

status.description: Delivery status of the test event (e.g. 'success', 'failed').

message.description: Human-readable description of the test outcome.

delivery_uuid.description: UUID of the delivery record created for this test.

RateLimitError.description: Body of a 429 response. The `Retry-After` header carries the same wait as `retry_after_seconds`. Only `detail` is always present.

detail.description: A human-readable message describing the error.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds until the request may be retried, when known.

scope.description: Which limit was hit, e.g. `burst`, `quota` or `payg_velocity`.

message.description: A human-readable explanation of the limit.

resolution.description: A human-readable hint on what to do next.

upgrade_url.description: Where to upgrade: the pay-as-you-go card page for free accounts, else the plans page (quota errors).

limit.description: The plan allowance that was used up (quota errors).

resets_on.description: UTC date the allowance resets (quota errors).

rate_limit.description: The per-minute limit that refused the request, e.g. `120/minute` (burst errors).

payg_url.description: Where to enable pay-as-you-go (quota and burst errors, when it applies).

dashboard_url.description: Where to see current spend (spend-cap and spend-ceiling errors).

contact_url.description: Where to ask for a higher limit (spend-cap and spend-ceiling errors).

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Server-to-server API key authentication. Provide your key in the `X-API-Key` request header. Keys can be generated and rotated from your account dashboard: https://financialfilings.com/profile/

CognitoJWT.description: AWS Cognito-issued JWT access token. Provide the token in the `Authorization` header as: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Tokens are issued via the Cognito hosted UI or the OAuth2 authorization code flow at `https://auth.financialreports.eu`.

post.description: Triggered when a filing has been successfully analyzed, classified, and converted to Markdown. This event contains the complete metadata and content.
Triggered immediately when a filing is ingested. Metadata (Filing Type, Language) and Markdown content may be null at this stage.

Sent when trigger_on_filing_updated is true and a filing you received was later re-typed or moved to another company. Same body as filing.processed, as the filing is now, plus 'changes'. Checked hourly over the last 30 days of deliveries (filings delivered since October 2026). Not billed.

Sent when a filing you received as filing.processed was later deleted or withdrawn, to every webhook whatever its flags; with trigger_on_filing_updated also while it is held back, or when it moved out of this webhook's scope. Discard the filing. Carries no filing or company body. Not billed.
Sent when trigger_on_dividend_events is true and a company in this webhook's scope announces a cash dividend. Requires a plan that includes structured financials. Not billed.
Sent when trigger_on_dividend_events is true and a later notice changes a dividend's stated dates, its stage or its cancellation. Same body as dividend.created, plus 'changes'. Not billed.
